programs.heading: Academic programs
programs.intro: Three performing arts degrees built on comprehensive, hands-on training grounded in the contemporary stage.

acting.title: Acting
desc: The Bachelor's Degree in Acting explores the craft from every angle the profession demands today: actor training, voice and physical expression; dramaturgy, history, philosophy, critical thinking and performance research; creation, laboratory work and staging; acting for camera, casting and dubbing; stagecraft, cultural management and the tools to understand how a stage project is created, produced and circulated. The curriculum also builds toward directing actors, executive production, entrepreneurship and research applied to the thesis project.
A curriculum to investigate, analyze, create, master different languages of performance, understand the technical resources of the stage and develop professional autonomy.

dance.title: Dance
desc: Contemporary Dance is the backbone of the degree. Around it, classical ballet, jazz, Caribbean rhythms, Mexican folklore and urban dance engage in dialogue with performance, choreographic composition, acting, voice, history, philosophy, critical thinking and research.

The training expands toward the languages and tools that build the contemporary stage: multimedia, space, light, set design and stagecraft; and toward the knowledge needed to develop and sustain projects: cultural management, the creative economy, funding, executive production and pedagogy for dance. The curriculum also includes functional anatomy and kinesiology, music applied to dance, audition management and a progressive choreographic lab process that culminates in the creation and staging of the thesis work.
A curriculum to perform, research, compose and create with technical mastery, critical thinking and a comprehensive understanding of the contemporary stage.

continuingEd.title: Continuing Studies
desc: Continuing Studies extends the OKAN Methodology beyond the degree programs. It is a space to specialize, update knowledge, professionalize a practice and discover new applications of stage tools in other fields of knowledge and work.

The offering combines training and professional development for performers; acting, dance, body and voice; philosophy and research in the arts; interdisciplinary creation; film and audiovisual media; martial arts applied to the stage; directing, production and company leadership; pedagogy and teacher training.

It also brings stage knowledge to other professional fields: training for speakers; presence and communication; leadership and teamwork; creativity and soft skills; tools applied to marketing, tourism and services; and preparing students and professionals to present, communicate and defend their projects.

Workshops, labs, courses, intensive programs and diplomas make it possible to build different paths according to each participant's experience, profession and goal. OKAN's agreements and partnerships expand this platform through collaboration with artists, specialists and institutions from other contexts, strengthening the national and international reach of its programs.

cta.text: Degree programs and Continuing Studies connected by the same way of learning: doing, thinking, researching, relating and creating.

admissions.heading: Admissions
admissions.intro: YOUR TRAINING AT OKAN STARTS HERE. We look for people ready to turn their interest in the performing arts into a professional training process.

welcome.title: WE WANT TO KNOW WHO YOU ARE AND HOW FAR YOU WANT TO TAKE YOUR TRAINING.
welcome.text: Admission begins with an interview. We want to learn about your interests, your experience, your expectations and your willingness to take on training that integrates practice, thinking, research and creation. Prior experience can be a starting point. The admissions process helps identify each applicant's stage of training and the corresponding entry path.

steps.title: INITIAL INTERVIEW
steps.desc: We get to know your profile, your interests and your educational background to guide your admission process.

steps.title: PREPARATORY TERM OR DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT
steps.desc: Admission includes crediting the preparatory term or, where applicable, a diagnostic assessment of prior knowledge. The Preparatory Term is part of OKAN's academic model: it diagnoses, levels and prepares the student for the start of the degree program.

steps.title: DOCUMENTATION
steps.desc: Submission and signing of the institutional regulations and required documentation, as well as a medical certificate or proof of physical fitness and health.

steps.title: ENROLLMENT
steps.desc: Complete the enrollment payment and formalize your entry into the OKAN community.

closing.title: START YOUR PROCESS.
closing.text: Two degree programs. One methodology. A professional education to build your path in the performing arts.

about.heading: About OKAN
about.intro: We are a School of the Arts where craft, thought, identity and creation are part of the same process. We train artists to understand what they do, discover their own voice and turn their practice into a profession.
about.missionText: To train performing artists with solid technical, creative, and intellectual tools, capable of researching, creating, and practicing their profession with identity, critical thinking, and awareness of their community and territory.
about.storyTitle: A SCHOOL THAT WAS BORN DOING.
about.storyText: OKAN was born from stage practice, training, and the need to build a space in Cancún for the professional training of artists. What began as a laboratory for creation and learning grew, questioned itself, and transformed into a School of the Arts with its own educational model. Today that story continues: training artists, generating knowledge, and building community from the Mexican Caribbean.

values.title: CRAFT
values.desc: Technical rigor and artistic discipline in every process.

values.title: THOUGHT
values.desc: An artist does not only create. They also question. History, dramaturgy, philosophy, analysis and research dialogue with practice to understand what we do, how and why.

values.title: IDENTITY
values.desc: We do not train artists to resemble others. Each process seeks for the student to recognize their tools, build judgment, and find their own artistic voice.

values.title: COMMUNITY AND TERRITORY
values.desc: Art does not happen isolated from the world. Training engages with its time, community, and territory to create, participate, and transform from within them.

agora.heading: Ágora OKAN
agora.intro: A space to talk and debate with guests.
agora.text: Ágora OKAN brings the school community together with artists, thinkers and special guests in open conversations that put stage practice in dialogue with the ideas that run through it.

laboratorio.heading: OKAN Laboratorio Escénico
laboratorio.text: OKAN's Stage Laboratory is the creation platform where students and artists develop, produce and present their own stage projects, taking classroom research into professional production.
